input.question: Why are indoor-only shopping malls dying in the USA?
input.ground_truth: Most indoor malls depend on the very large "anchor" stores to pull people in. These are your Macy's, Nordstrom, and other department stores, for the most part. These stores aren't doing nearly as well with the advent of online shopping, so the foot traffic to the other stores suffer. With less foot traffic, the smaller stores start to shutter, and it becomes a cycle. Strip malls are significantly less expensive and don't depend on their anchor stores in the same way.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: Why are indoor-only shopping malls dying in the USA?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you have a big toy box at home where you can play with toys, but you can’t go outside and play in the park or visit your friend’s house. That would get boring after a while, right?

Shopping malls used to be like that big toy box for grown-ups. They had lots of stores to visit and places to eat, all under one roof. But now, people can go online and buy almost anything they want from their phones or computers, just like you can watch cartoons on your tablet at home.

Also, people want to go outside and walk around, or visit fun places like parks, restaurants, or stores that are spread out in a neighborhood, not just in one big building. These places are called “open-air” places, and they are more fun and fresh because you can feel the air and see the sky.

So, because people can shop online and like going to places where they can move around outside, the big indoor-only shopping malls are not as popular anymore. That’s why they are “dying.”
